turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is... work is just getting really difficult. I manage a health clinic, so I have to do all these EPIC quality reports. Which, by the way, EPIC has been an absolute nightmare since the system update last weekend. Our IT guy, Dave, swore it was going to make the billing codes easier to pull, but half the nursing staff got locked out on Monday morning and I spent three hours just on hold with the vendor. It's always something with the software, you know? My husband told me I shouldn't take my work stress home, but it's hard not to when the system is always crashing. 

But, um, anyway, the actual problem is that I can start one of those EPIC reports, or sit down in a clinic metrics meeting with every intention of tracking it, and... within just a few minutes, my mind has drifted so far that I’m just rereading the exact same numbers over and over. Or I'll suddenly realize I completely missed the entire point of the discussion. It's just happening way too much.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly describes an inability to sustain attention during tasks like reading reports or sitting in meetings, noting that their mind drifts within minutes and they have to reread numbers or miss the discussion.

turns.doctor_question: Looking back to childhood, did you already have trouble paying attention or staying focused?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, yeah, definitely. Even back in elementary school, I remember teachers always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. My mother hated that word. She actually kept all those old report cards in this big cedar chest at the foot of her bed. I still have that chest, actually in my guest room. When she passed away a few years ago, my sister really wanted it, but she lives in this tiny condo up in Chicago and there was just no way it was going to fit. Have you ever tried moving solid wood furniture into a Chicago walk-up? The stairwells are impossibly narrow. We ended up having to hire these specialized movers just to get her couch in, and it cost an absolute fortune. I told her she should just buy things flat-packed, but she loves antiques, so... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, childhood focus. Yeah, so because of the whole focus thing, my mother actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night while I finished my homework. If she didn't literally sit right there, I would just completely lose track of my assignments, or I'd realize I forgot my books at school and we'd have to go back and get them.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient recalls elementary school teachers writing on report cards that they were 'careless'.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly confirms the doctor's question about having trouble paying attention and staying focused since childhood.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient states they would lose track of assignments and fail to finish homework unless their mother sat with them.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient mentions frequently forgetting their books at school, which are necessary items for completing homework.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by a chain of unrelated thoughts about a cedar chest and moving furniture, causing them to forget the doctor's question.

turns.doctor_question: Do you notice this same trouble staying focused in other parts of your life besides work?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, definitely. Outside of work, I do a lot of... or I used to do a lot of volunteer health workshops in the community. We hold them at the rec center over on 4th street. Which, by the way, they just completely remodeled the lobby there and put in this incredible new espresso machine. It's one of those fancy Italian ones with the double boiler? My husband actually bought me a burr grinder for Christmas because he is absolutely obsessed with coffee. He orders these special beans from a tiny roaster in Seattle, and he insists that pre-ground coffee is the reason I always get heartburn. He’s probably right, honestly, but who has the time to manually grind beans every single morning when you're already running late? I mean, the noise alone wakes up our dog, and then she starts barking at the window, and it's just a whole ordeal before 7 AM... 

Wait, I completely lost my train of thought. I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh! The workshops. Right. 

So, yeah, I actually had to step back from leading parts of those volunteer workshops recently. I just can't reliably keep all the planning pieces moving anymore. I'd sit down to organize the schedule and just completely zone out. And honestly, it's getting really bad at the clinic, too. My delays are actually starting to affect our reporting deadlines. It’s awful because I'm making other teams wait on me to finish my part, and I just... I can't seem to stay focused long enough to get it done on time.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states they cannot stay focused long enough to complete their tasks on time.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports failing to finish workplace duties, resulting in missed reporting deadlines and making other teams wait.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes an inability to reliably keep planning pieces moving and organize schedules for volunteer workshops.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by going off on a tangent about coffee and their dog, completely losing their train of thought mid-sentence.
symptom_reasoning.S059: The patient describes their mind going blank, stating they 'completely zone out' when sitting down to organize.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel restless or like you need to keep moving, even when you’re supposed to sit still?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, I can sit still just fine. It's my husband who's the restless one. He can never just sit and watch a movie with me. He's always getting up to check his phone, or puttering around in the kitchen, or deciding right in the middle of a scene that he absolutely has to organize the garage. Which, honestly, the garage is a total disaster area right now. We had all these boxes left over from when we redid the downstairs bathroom last fall. The contractor we used was terrible, just the worst. He promised it would take three weeks, and it ended up taking two months, and he left dust everywhere. I swear I'm still finding drywall dust on the baseboards. We should have just gone with the guy my sister recommended, but he was booked out until spring... 

But, um, anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, moving around. No, I don't really have that problem. I can sit in my chair for hours, it's just that my brain is a million miles away.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient notes that while sitting still, her 'brain is a million miles away,' indicating distraction by unrelated thoughts.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly denies having trouble staying seated, stating she 'can sit in my chair for hours.'
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly denies feeling restless or needing to move around, stating she 'can sit still just fine.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
turns.patient_response:
No, I wouldn't say I worry all the time. I mean, I worry about normal things, like my husband's cholesterol or whether the dog is getting enough exercise. She's a rescue, you know, a mix of terrier and something else, maybe beagle? The shelter wasn't really sure. We got her about five years ago, right around the time my husband's mother moved into that assisted living place over in Westlake. That place is beautiful, honestly. They have a whole dining room that looks like a high-end restaurant, and they do these weekly outings to the symphony and the art museum. I always tell my husband I want to move in there when I'm older. The food is actually really good, too. They had this roasted salmon dish last time we visited that was perfectly cooked, which is so hard to do for a large group. I tried to recreate it at home, but I think my oven runs a little hot, because the edges got all dry...

Wait, sorry. Worrying. No, I don't think I'm an overly anxious person. I just get frustrated when I can't get my work done, but I don't sit around worrying about bad things happening or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by her own unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about her dog, mother-in-law, and cooking before catching herself and returning to the question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, rambling response detailing unrelated stories before answering the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying excessively or being an overly anxious person.

turns.doctor_question: When did your trouble focusing start getting noticeably worse?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it really started getting noticeably worse about two years and four months ago. That's when I got promoted at the clinic. Before that, I had these little systems that worked fine, you know? But then they gave me this much larger portfolio to manage, and it just completely overwhelmed everything I used to rely on. 

It was right around the same time my sister bought her new house, actually. She moved out to the suburbs, which I told her was a mistake because the commute is just brutal. She spends at least an hour on the freeway every morning, and you know how traffic gets around here. Plus, she bought this older house that needs so much work. The plumbing is a nightmare. She had a pipe burst in the guest bathroom just a week after she moved in, and it flooded the whole hallway. They had to rip up the original hardwood floors, which was such a shame because they were gorgeous. Real oak, not that laminate stuff everyone uses now. I always wanted hardwood floors in our bedroom, but my husband says carpet is better for the winter. He gets cold feet at night, so he wears these thick wool socks to bed...

Oh, I'm sorry, I'm doing it again. But yeah, the focus issues... it was the promotion. Two years and four months ago. That's when it all really started falling apart for me.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly confirms having 'focus issues' and 'trouble focusing' that worsened after her promotion.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes how managing a larger portfolio completely overwhelmed the systems she used to rely on, indicating difficulty organizing tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about her sister's house and husband's socks before catching herself.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
No, I haven't really felt down or depressed like that. I mean, I get frustrated, obviously, with work and everything, but not sad. My mood is usually pretty okay. 

Actually, speaking of moods, my neighbor just got this new puppy, a golden retriever, and you cannot be sad around that dog. He is just the happiest little thing. But he barks constantly when she leaves for work. She works at the bank downtown, the one with the big clock tower? They just renovated the lobby there, and it looks so modern now, all glass and steel. I don't really like it, honestly. I prefer the old architecture, like the library on 4th street. They have those amazing stone lions out front. My grandfather used to take me there when I was little, and we would spend hours in the children's section... 

Um, but no, I'm not depressed. Just... scattered, I guess. But not down in the dumps.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes feeling 'scattered' and demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts during their response.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from the topic of their mood to a neighbor's puppy, a bank, architecture, and a library before returning to the question.
symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling down, sad, or depressed.
